scope: Focused independent documentary/source review of MCP23008 IO7 direction/readback, no implementation edits or physical/device/production execution.
conclusion: Program IODIR bit7 to0 for MCP23008, even when GP7 is NC. Verify the complete documented expected IODIR byte; do not mask bit7 to accommodate a conjectured readback. The current SW2-J4 code already uses legal0x7F and its full-byte/trailing read check must be retained.

documented_vs_unknown.documented: DS20001919I printed p.9 Register1-1 labels IO7 R/W-1. The notation defines it as readable/writable with POR1; it is not U/unimplemented/read-as-zero. The explicit MCP23008 note requires writing IO7=0. The legal programmed state therefore expects bit7 readback0 by the register contract.
documented_vs_unknown.not_claimed: No device was measured. The result of deliberately writing unsupported IO7=1 is not inferred or relied on. Output-only pin functionality does not establish a read-as-zero register bit. No undocumented silicon behavior or automatic masking workaround is assumed.
documented_vs_unknown.revision_history: AppendixA printed p.40 attributes feature/pin/IODIR correction to G (June2022); H (November2025) concerns package drawings; I (February2026) corrects Byte/Sequential Read Figure1-1. The IO7 requirement is not introduced by the February2026 framing change.
documented_vs_unknown.errata: Official DS80251A is a2005 Rev.A erratum about false I2C address ACKs for A1/prior, fixed in A2/date0543 and later. It does not redefine IO7 readback. No primary IO7 erratum altering Register1-1 was found in the reviewed sources. For a new two-device bus, this ancient address-decoder issue is a separate assembly/revision sourcing consideration.

current_source_corrections.IODIR: The current source and preflight snapshot configure0x7F, not0xFF.
current_source_corrections.GP7_usage: Existing0x20 SW2-J4 uses GP7 as a challenge output through1k to GP6 with100k pull-down. Acquisition alternates OLAT bit7 and verifies GPIO bit6. GP7 NC applies to the proposed0x21 LED, not this current accessory.
current_source_corrections.guard: Both the register-block IODIR and separately reread trailing IODIR compare the full expected0x7F byte. Masking bit7 would accept reset0xFF for that direction check and weaken the mid-read reset guard.

new_LED_recommendation.policy: Preload a safe OLAT value, then program an explicit IODIR byte with bit7 clear, and verify that full byte along with other owned configuration/latch state. GP7 remains physically NC and is not used as an input/health signal.
new_LED_recommendation.example_only: If GP0..2 are outputs and GP3..6 inputs, IODIR=(~0x07)&0x7F=0x78. If unused pins are also outputs, choose the corresponding explicit value. Exact LED polarity and unused-pin plan remain hardware/driver design choices, not a released configuration.

locators: p.9 Register1-1 R/W-1 and explicit IO7 output note
p.1 I2C false-ACK issue, no IO7 clarification

retrieval_limit: An alternate official filename ending MCP23008-and-MCP23S08-Data-Sheet-DS20001919.pdf returned HTTP403 during local retrieval. Its web search extract identifies RevisionH; no conclusion requires that unavailable snapshot. The successfully downloaded current RevisionI and its own revision history are authoritative for this review.
physical_gate: A future separately authorized bench test should confirm legal direction write/read, POR/reset detection, GPIO/OLAT loopback and part marking under the assembly supply. This review does not replace that test.
